Bevacizumab is directly linked to the Low affinity immunoglobulin gamma Fc region receptor II-a, which in turn is targeted by both alemtuzumab and benfotiamine. Alemtuzumab, a drug that targets the same receptor, is known to interact with Lymphotoxin-alpha, while benfotiamine also exerts a target effect on this protein. The scores from the two paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in the relationship between bevacizumab and Lymphotoxin-alpha, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains unclear. The evidence suggests that the Low affinity immunoglobulin gamma Fc region receptor II-a may act as a common intermediary in the signaling pathways of these drugs, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between bevacizumab and Lymphotoxin-alpha.
